subject: Follow-up: Post-demo probe plan + A/B latency/throughput tests
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chan <emily@dataforge.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Apr 2029 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Post-demo probe plan + A/B latency/throughput tests

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap + suggested next steps so we stay aligned on what will move the evaluation forward: 

Summary from our call
- You ran the sample workload against your current inference endpoint (on-prem + hyperscaler fallback). You care most about p95/p99 latency for 512-token completion, and steady-state tokens/sec for batched requests.
- Procurement will want a clear SLA and a predictable cost model before committing.

Proposed probe plan (what Redwood will run / coordinate)
1) A/B latency test (3rd party harness):
   - Workload: 512 token completions, 50% streaming, 50% non-streaming
   - Metrics: p50/p95/p99, tail jitter, 95% of requests under X ms (we'll set targets after one warmup run)
2) Throughput ramp (tokens/sec):
   - Progressive concurrency ramps (1, 4, 8, 16 inference streams) to identify sustained tokens/sec and mem pressure points
3) Fallback/degenerate path verification:
   - Simulate partial availability of hyperscaler regions and assert Redwood routing fallback latency delta

Differentiators we'll validate vs Hyperscaler API
- Consistent p95 under mixed streaming workloads (reduces jitter by batching + KV caching)
- Predictable reserved capacity behavior under sustained tokens/sec loads
- Transparent cost delta at token-level for each test configuration (we'll produce a cost breakdown)

What I need from you to schedule the lab next week
- Confirm the target p95/p99 objectives (or tell us your procurement thresholds)
- Provide a point of contact for network path and firewall rules (we'll need IP allowlist for the test harness)
- Procurement contact for the SLA draft review (I attached a starter SLA and the probe spreadsheet)

Attachments: 20290412-probe-metrics.xlsx (test matrix + expected measurements), dataforge-sla-draft.pdf (starter SLA)

If that looks good, I propose we run the A/B latency sweep Tue/Wed next week (Apr 16–17). I’ll own the test harness coordination; Aditya will own results analysis; Marissa will coordinate procurement/SLA items.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Emily Chan <emily@dataforge.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@dataforge.ai
Date: Fri, 12 Apr 2029 17:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Post-demo probe plan + A/B latency/throughput tests

Thanks Kimberly — appreciate the clear plan. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Procurement thresholds: our bar for p95 is currently 220 ms for 512-token streamed completions (we are flexible if the cost delta justifies it). They want p99 under 450 ms.
- Network: our infra team (cc’d) will need the test harness IPs to allowlist. Can you confirm whether the tests originate from Redwood’s hosted region or from the test harness in our account?
- Cost visibility: procurement wants a per-test cost estimate and a breakdown by model variant + quantization.

We’ll review the SLA draft this afternoon and get back with edits. If you can confirm the origin of the test traffic and share a lightweight cost estimate based on the spreadsheet, we can lock in Tue/Wed.

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 13 Apr 2029 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Follow-up: Post-demo probe plan + A/B latency/throughput tests

Kimberly — quick ops notes and a proposed split of responsibilities before we kick off:

Ops assumptions
- Test harness: we'll run the latency A/B from Redwood-hosted runners that can be deployed in the same cloud region as DataForge's hyperscaler fallback (reduces cross-region noise). We will provide allowlist IPs 24 hours before runs.
- Models: default run will use the customer-selected 13B family model (quantized fp4), then a 7B fallback run for cost comparison.
- Measurement tooling: we’ll use k6 + a lightweight trace collector to capture per-request timings and KV cache hit rates.

Who does what
- Kimberly: finalize schedule with Emily and procurement, own customer comms
- Marissa: lead SLA discussion and get procurement’s hard thresholds; own legal routing on SLA edits
- Me (Aditya): set up test harness, provide runner IPs, run warmup and capture raw logs, produce analysis artifacts (p50/p95/p99 csv + tokens/sec curves)

Targets we should aim for to make a strong case vs hyperscaler
- p95 <= 200 ms for 512-token streamed completions for the 13B quantized run
- p99 <= 420 ms
- Sustained tokens/sec above 15k for 8 concurrent streams across reserved capacity

I’ll prepare the runner playbook and push the IPs to the Drive link by EOD Mon. Noted — procurement wants per-test cost; I’ll estimate core-hours and token units per the spreadsheet.

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Post-demo probe plan + A/B latency/throughput tests — schedule confirmed

Emily / team —

Thanks for the quick responses. Per the items above we are confirmed to run the A/B latency sweep on Apr 16th and throughput ramps on Apr 17th. Action summary: 

1) Network allowlist
   - Aditya will drop the Redwood runner IPs to the Drive doc by Mon EOD (we’ll also paste them here once posted). Please have infra confirm allowlist by 06:00 PDT on Apr 16th.
2) SLA draft
   - Marissa to coordinate edits with procurement. Procurement: please flag any non-starters in the PDF.
3) Cost estimate
   - Aditya will post a per-test estimate (core-hours + token units) in the Drive file before the run.
4) Test ownership
   - Redwood run owner: Aditya Rao (raw logs + analysis)
   - Customer contact for validation: Emily Chan
   - Commercial leads: Kimberly Park / Marissa Cole

Acceptance targets we’ll report against in the summary deck
- p95 target (13B quantized): 200 ms (goal) / 220 ms (acceptable)
- p99 target: 420 ms (goal) / 450 ms (acceptable)
- Sustained tokens/sec goal (8 streams): >= 15k tokens/sec

Links & attachments:
- Probe matrix: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-probe-doc (Aditya will update with IPs and estimates)
- HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/DF-2029-112
- Attachments: 20290412-probe-metrics.xlsx, dataforge-sla-draft.pdf

Sam — looping in Hypercloud to keep them informed of the interop test plan. If Redwood’s runner traffic needs to come from a specific hyperscaler region for parity, we’ll coordinate that during the warmup.

If anything changes, flag it here. Otherwise we’ll post runner IPs and the preliminary cost estimate by EOD Mon.

Best —
